lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Rebuilt weekly carrier scorecards used by 6 regional managers to renegotiate contracts, cutting late deliveries from 11% to 7% in two quarters.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing, Python
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Check that the LinkedIn URL is live and the email and voicemail are professional.
Clarify whether “under 5 days” was your individual contribution or a team/service standard.
items.because: The distinction makes the claim more credible.

items.says: Add a concrete result for the hydraulic-systems work if you have one.
items.because: Otherwise it reads mainly as a duty.

items.says: Clarify what the “single verification step” changed.
items.because: The description could sound as though verification requirements were removed.

items.says: Check whether “shipping it to all merchants” matches the pilot-region scope elsewhere.
Distinguish a 5-percentage-point increase from a 5% increase.
Support tickets a feature would close are not necessarily its RICE Reach.
items.because: They are not necessarily the number of users or merchants reached.

items.says: State the Reach measure and its time period accurately, including that tickets “would close” is a prediction.
items.because: That wording implies a predicted outcome.

items.says: Specify the roadmap decision or priority that resulted.
items.because: The research and analysis are shown, but what changed is missing.

items.says: Consider combining this bullet with the RICE bullet if both describe the same decision.
Session-level randomization does not establish the stated effect on merchants’ customers.
items.because: Sessions were randomized, and customers may have had multiple sessions.

items.says: The A/B-test bullet repeats the checkout-conversion result.
items.because: Methodological detail should add something the earlier bullet does not.

items.says: Clarify whether the two-region rollout was approved, funded, or completed.
items.because: Those are different claims.

items.says: Clarify how the scorecards contributed to fewer late deliveries.
items.because: The mechanism connecting contract renegotiations to late-delivery rates is not obvious.

items.says: Make your role in the rollout clear.
Replace the switch to “my redesign.”
items.because: It is inconsistent with the rest of the résumé’s style.

items.says: Check that the forecast-error figures use the same definition and period.
Separate or trim the distinct contributions in the route-planning bullet.
items.because: Their number makes the source of the 1,800-hour saving hard to identify.

items.says: Clarify whether 3,100 students used the app or merely had access to it.
Tie the “first year” timeframe clearly to the nine-tonne figure.
The increase from 400 to 1,150 is 187.5%, not 150%.
Ensure the reminders can reasonably be credited with the increase.
items.because: They may have simply coincided with it.

items.says: The increase from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not an unqualified 20%.
items.because: The relative increase is about 26.7%.

items.says: Clarify how the volunteer shift system affected pickup-slot fill rate.
Distinguish modeled potential savings from realized savings.
items.because: Pilot funding is a separate outcome.

items.says: Replace the passive framing with your specific contribution.
Clarify whether the shortened form was implemented at all four clinics.
items.because: The scope is ambiguous as written.

items.says: The pilot-approval outcome repeats the first practicum bullet.
items.because: The space could show a distinct finding or contribution.

items.says: Separate Python from product practices.
items.because: The categories would make more sense.

items.says: Make Harbor Payments the most detailed role and prioritize product decisions and measurable app outcomes.
items.because: The measured Harbor Payments work is the strongest evidence for product roles.

items.says: Keep the mechanic role brief for product applications.
items.because: It explains current work but need not crowd out more relevant experience.
